shots.text: Pepsi's ad showed a fighter jet as a prize.
You see, in nineteen ninety-six, Pepsi Points could get you T-shirts and leather jackets.
At the end of the ad, a teenager lands a Harrier jet at his school.
On screen it said: seven million Pepsi Points.
A twenty-one-year-old business student near Seattle did the math.
The rules let you buy extra points for ten cents each.
Seven million points would cost him about seven hundred thousand dollars.
A real Harrier was worth more than twenty million dollars.
So he got investors to lend him seven hundred thousand dollars.
He mailed Pepsi fifteen points and a check for the rest.
But Pepsi sent the check back and said the jet was only there to be funny.
Then in nineteen ninety-nine, a judge ruled no reasonable person could think the ad was serious.
And Pepsi's new ad? The jet now cost seven hundred million points.
